newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Export of most Colombia coffee delayed until Feb.2.
newsitem.headline: Export of most Colombia coffee delayed until Feb.2.

text.p: The bulk of Colombia's coffee exports will be delayed until at least February 2 as moves get under way to redirect shipments from the strike-bound port of Buenaventura to other ports, private exporters said Wednesday.

The National Coffee Growers' Federation sent a letter to exporters Wednesday authorizing them to start returning coffee to processors. The consignments will then have to be unloaded, rechecked and dispatched to Colombia's Caribbean coast ports.

The dock workers' strike at Buenaventura went into its eighth day Wednesday and despite on-going talks, no immediate end was in sight. It is not clear how much coffee exporters will opt to pull out of the port and redirect for shipment.

Federation officials said last week 90,000 60-kg bags were still loaded on trucks in or just outside the port. Private exporters say they have 145,000 60-kg bags blocked by the industrial action but were unable to say how much of that was on trucks and how much in warehouses at dockside.
A private exporter said that by the time loads were returned to processors, checked and redirected through Santa Marta, Barranquilla or Cartagena it would be at least Feb. 2.
About 60 percent of all Colombia's coffee exports are shipped through Buenaventura. A total of more than 300,000 60-kg bags of coffee destined for export has been snarled by the stoppage.
Given the federation's tight control of the Colombian coffee industry, exporters had to wait until it gave the green light before they could begin pulling out truckloads of coffee from Buenaventura.
In a separate development, the powerful Colombian Truck Drivers' Association began billing exporters $3,000 for the time they have spent waiting at dockside, unable to off-load their cargoes.
It was not immediately known how many trucks are waiting but federation officials said there were at least 180 snarled in the strike last week.
